Q: Failed to get access token from MSAL python library A:

To connect with Microsoft Graph API via application, make use of acquire_token_for_client flow.

  • acquire_token_silent is used to get a token from the cache if it exists. It is used in scenarios where you have an interactive user session and want to silently obtain a new token without prompting the user again.

I created a Microsoft Entra ID application and granted API permissions:

Hence, to get the access token modify the code like below:

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
#from flask_cors import CORS
import logging
from msal import ConfidentialClientApplication

app = Flask(__name__)
#CORS(app)

client_id="ClientID"
client_secret="ClientSecret"
tenant_id="TenantID"

msal_authority = f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}"

scopes = ['https://graph.microsoft.com/.default']

msal_app = ConfidentialClientApplication(
    client_id=client_id,
    client_credential=client_secret,
    authority=msal_authority
)

result = msal_app.acquire_token_for_client(scopes=scopes)

if "access_token" in result:
    access_token = result['access_token']
    print("Access token ==================> ", access_token)
else:
    raise Exception("No Access Token Found: " + result.get("error_description", "Unknown error"))

Access token retrieved successfully:

When decoded the roles are displayed:

Using the above generated access token, you can call Microsoft Graph API.

Q: Jupyter notebook refusing to recognize matplotlib installation A:

VS Code has official support for Jupyter Notebooks.

I would recommend creating a new empty directory so you can start the setup process from scratch if you can, as it is often easier than fixing something after it has gone wrong (which tends to cause unpredictable knock-on effects which propagate the error!).

Next, open the empty folder in VS Code with code path/to/my/folder. Create a test.ipynb file inside and open it - VS Code should recognise the file type and customise the editor with Jupyter-specific options.

At this stage in the top-right corner you will see a Select Kernel button: follow the options to create a new virtual environment - this will generate a .venv inside your folder.

Finally, use Ctrl+Shift+P to run the View: Toggle Terminal command: it will open a shell in the directory you opened VS Code in, which contains the .venv folder.

Now inside the shell you can run . .\.ven\bin\activate to enter the Python environment the VS Code Jupyter kernel will be using, and install matplotlib inside it with pip install matplotlib.

I did this on Linux earlier today, but the instructions I have provided should work on Windows - in any case please reply to the answer if you encounter any issues.

Q: Can it be reasonable to use custom instead of standard datatype, if otherwise you'd need many instances of custom iterator? A:

Thanks a lot for that very differentiated and well explained answer.

Just to explain my assessment: Actually, I'd gladly use standard data types as it would help my co-workers a lot. The main Problem is not only the circular behaviour, but the fact that the algorithms do not only constantly navigate through polygons (at different positions), they also rearrange the polygons (insert or cut items). The fact, that all the iterators would have to stay valid all the time, is what's challenging me the most.

Q: Can QGIS server read projects from database A:

Not sure if you still need an answer, but I found this solution to be able to read dynamically qgis project stored in PostgreSQL database :

docker-compose.yaml

services:
  qgisserver:
    image: qgis/qgis-server:latest
    volumes:
      - ./:/io/data
      - ./pg_service.conf:/etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf:ro 
      - ./qgis_nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    environment:
      - QGIS_SERVER_LOG_LEVEL=0
      - DEBUG=1
      - QGIS_USER=1000
      - PGSERVICEFILE=/etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf 
    ports:
      - "4003:80"
  postgis:
    image: postgis/postgis:18-3.6-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $$POSTGRES_USER -d $$POSTGRES_DB"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=geodata
      - POSTGRES_USER=georchestra
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=georchestra
    volumes:
      - ./volumes/postgis_data:/var/lib/postgresql
    ports:
      - 5432:5432

pg_service.conf

[geodata]
host=postgis
port=5432
dbname=geodata
user=georchestra
password=georchestra

nginx.qgis.conf add this from the original one

        location /test/ {
            rewrite ^/test/(.*)$ /qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi?project=$1;
        } 
        location /qgis/ {
            internal; # Used only by the OGC rewrite
            root /var/www/data;
            fastcgi_pass  localhost:9993;

            fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;
            fastcgi_param QUERY_STRING    $query_string;
            # build links in GetCapabilities based on
            # the hostname exposed by the reverse proxy
            fastcgi_param  HTTPS $qgis_ssl;
            fastcgi_param  SERVER_NAME $qgis_host;
            fastcgi_param  SERVER_PORT $qgis_port;
            fastcgi_param  QGIS_PROJECT_FILE "postgresql:///?service=geodata&schema=projects&project=$arg_project";
            fastcgi_param  MAP "postgresql:///?service=geodata&schema=projects&project=$arg_project";
            include fastcgi_params;
        }

Create two projects in the database name bati and test

Open URLs:

  • http://localhost:4003/test/bati?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0%20&REQUEST=GetCapabilities
  • http://localhost:4003/test/test?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0%20&REQUEST=GetCapabilities
